findings.summary: Naming all nine intro sections creates 13 landmarks, including the closing promotional call to action, making screen-reader landmark navigation unnecessarily verbose.
findings.fix: Remove aria-labelledby from the closing call-to-action section, hero, prototype notice, and ordinary narrative sections where heading navigation is sufficient; retain each heading and its ID. Reserve named regions for essential navigable destinations.

passed: Native anchors, buttons, details/summary, headings, lists and landmarks express the controls without redundant roles.
Without JavaScript all eight guide contents remain visible and the unavailable global toggle stays hidden.
Each enhanced step button has an accessible heading-derived name, valid aria-controls and aria-expanded synchronized with panel.hidden.
The global toggle references all eight existing panel IDs and updates its label, expanded state and polite status message.
Hash navigation reveals the destination and same-page hash changes focus its step button; repeated links to the current hash reopen a collapsed destination.
Guide navigation landmarks have distinct names; current-page navigation uses aria-current=page.
Decorative SVGs and redundant toggle words are hidden from assistive technology.
The single added login link is a native anchor with a clear Korean accessible name.
notes: Static source review only; browser focus behavior and actual VoiceOver/NVDA announcements were not exercised.
